name: Coredump Console
status: server endpoints + page implemented; device side (firmware on another machine) is the uploader — see /docs/coredump-upload.md
description: Web console for ESP32 crash-dump collection: list coredumps uploaded by devices on boot, show panic reason / crashing task / firmware version / receive time, and download the raw dump for offline symbolization. All data comes from the live API — no mock data. Upload is device-side (no Bearer token; the MAC is the identity). The server stores raw bytes to disk keyed by sha256 and dedups on (deviceId, sha256).
description_zh: ESP32 崩溃转储收集台：查看设备开机上传的 coredump 列表（崩溃原因/崩溃任务/固件版本/接收时间），下载原始 dump 供离线符号化。数据全部来自服务器实时接口，页面内无假数据；上报由设备端完成（免鉴权，MAC 即身份）；服务器按 sha256 落盘、按 (deviceId, sha256) 幂等排重。
canonical_url_hint: Share the full base URL including the path /coredump (host is the shared firmware-server)

upload.auth: device-side (no Bearer token by design — the MAC is the identity)

query.sha256: required — sha256 of the raw body bytes (64 hex)
query.size: optional — byte count; if given must equal body length

headers.X-Panic-Reason: optional — urlencoded panic reason (<=2KB), server decodes it
headers.X-App-Elf-Sha256: optional — sha256 of the crashing app ELF (64 hex), for symbolization

upload.returns: { ok: true, id: 'cdump_...', duplicate: false } or { ok: true, id: '<existing id>', duplicate: true }

errors.400: bad deviceId / sha256 missing or not 64 hex / empty body / sha256 does not match body / size mismatch

upload.note: at-least-once semantics: the server dedups on (deviceId, sha256) and returns duplicate:true on repeat, so a retry after a lost ack does not create a second record. sha256 is recomputed from the body and must match — this also guards against transmission corruption and naive spoofing.

list.returns: { _meta: { service, docs, maxPerDevice }, coredumps: Coredump[] } — newest first, each with downloadUrl

errors.404: not found / dump file missing on server

Coredump.sha256: sha256 of the raw body bytes (64 hex) — the dedup key
Coredump.panicReason: string | null — already decoded on the server
Coredump.appElfSha256: string | null — crashing app ELF sha256, for symbolization
Coredump.receivedAt: ISO8601 UTC — receive time (the crash absolute time is NOT recoverable from the dump)
Coredump.downloadUrl: string — /api/coredumps/{id}/download (absolute when listed via the page)

invariants: at-least-once upload; server dedups on (deviceId, sha256) and returns duplicate:true
sha256 is the signature of the raw body bytes; server recomputes and rejects mismatch (400)
dump bytes are stored to disk as <sha256>.bin — not embedded in the JSON store
retention: at most 20 coredumps per device; oldest evicted together with its dump file
receive time (receivedAt) is the only trustworthy timestamp — the dump has no wall-clock time
symbolization is offline (espcoredump.py + matching app ELF), never in the page

auth.upload_guards: deviceId whitelist (12 lower-hex), body <= 64K, sha256 must match body — three hard checks against disk flooding over the unauthenticated binary endpoint
auth.known_trust_boundary: over plain HTTP anyone can spoof any deviceId to upload fake data (same existing limitation as the OTA report endpoint)

data_source.mock: none — the page contains no built-in fake data

not_implemented: online symbolization in the page (offline only, see /docs/coredump.md §7)
device-side firmware uploader (lives in another repository; see /docs/coredump-upload.md)
automatic symbol matching against the registry (appElfSha256 is stored but not yet auto-resolved)
